conclusion_installation: A ~0.993 m inextensible cable lying on the table, one end anchored at (0.05, 0), the other end held by the tool; 20 markers along it. The task is cable routing: lay the cable on the prescribed side of three pegs and park the end at the target. The load is the cable tension at the tool: friction/drag of the cable sliding on the table, increasing with drag speed and with the length of cable being slid around pegs (capstan-like); ~0.2-0.9 N residual at rest. The geometry always leaves 0.14-0.29 m of slack, so failures are dynamic, never geometric.
field_note_refers_to: 'Fights back when you hurry' = rate-dependent drag: the faster the cable is pulled (especially when wrapped around pegs) the higher the tension; and a tool jammed against a peg that breaks free rushes to its servo reference, giving tension spikes of 11-21 N.
